questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Describe the resolution of a monitor. (1 mark)

(b) Give TWO advantages of LCD monitors over CRT monitors. (2 marks)

(c) Give the role of graphic controllers in the resolution of a monitor. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Resolution (1 mark)**

The resolution of a monitor is the **number of pixels (picture elements) displayed across the width and the height of the screen**, for example $1920 \times 1080$. The **more pixels, the sharper and more detailed the picture**.

**(b) Two advantages of LCD over CRT (2 marks)**

- An LCD monitor is **thin, light and takes little desk space**, and is easy to move.
- It **uses much less power and gives off less heat**, has **no flicker and less eye strain**, and its screen is flat and sharp. (Other acceptable points: no harmful radiation, longer life.)

**(c) Role of the graphics controller (1 mark)**

The graphics controller (graphics card / video adapter) **processes the image data from the CPU and converts it into the signals sent to the monitor**, using its **video memory**; the amount of video memory and the power of the controller **determine the maximum resolution and the number of colours** that the monitor can show.

questions.enonce_markdown:
To send documents, companies sometimes use social media, ordinary post office, or emails.

(a) Give TWO reasons why social media might be used. (2 marks)

(b) Give TWO reasons why ordinary post might be used. (2 marks)

(c) Give TWO advantages in using the above means. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Two reasons for using social media (2 marks)**

- It is **instant and free (or very cheap)**: the document reaches the receiver at once, whatever the distance.
- It **reaches many people at the same time** (groups, pages) and **most customers and staff already use it**; files can be attached and replies are immediate.

**(b) Two reasons for using ordinary post (2 marks)**

- The **original, signed paper document** is delivered (contracts, certificates, cheques, legal notices), which is **legally accepted as proof**, with a recorded delivery if needed.
- It **needs no Internet connection or device** at the receiver's end and is **safe from hackers and malware**; it is the only way to reach people who do not have e-mail, and it can carry **parcels and samples**.

**(c) Two advantages of using the above means (2 marks)**

- They are **convenient and cheap** compared with delivering documents by hand, and the sender does not have to travel.
- They **reach a wide audience** and leave a **record (evidence)** that the document was sent, while e-mail and social media are also **fast**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give THREE ways in which a system analyst can gather information to design a new system for an organization. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Three fact-finding methods (3 marks)**

1. **Interviews**: the analyst questions managers and users face to face to get detailed information and opinions about the present system and the requirements.
2. **Questionnaires**: written questions given to many users or customers, a quick and cheap way to collect information from a large number of people.
3. **Observation**: the analyst watches the staff at work in order to see how the present system is really used and where the problems are.
4. **Document (record) inspection**: the study of forms, reports, manuals and files in use (this may replace one of the three above).

(Any three correct methods earn the 3 marks; research on similar systems and group meetings are also accepted.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A health facility decides to use an expert system to facilitate its operations.

(a) What is an expert system? (2 marks)

(b) Name TWO basic elements of an expert system. (1 mark)

(c) Give ONE area in health where experts system is used. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Expert system (2 marks)**

An expert system is a **computer program that imitates the knowledge and the reasoning of a human expert in one particular field**. It asks the user questions and, by applying **rules to a store of facts about the subject**, it **gives advice, a diagnosis or a decision**, often explaining how it reached it.

**(b) Two basic elements (1 mark)**

The **knowledge base** (the facts and the if-then rules supplied by experts) and the **inference engine** (the part that reasons with the rules to reach conclusions). (Also acceptable: the **user interface** and the **explanation facility**.)

**(c) One area in health (1 mark)**

**Medical diagnosis**: the system proposes the likely disease from the symptoms and test results entered by the nurse or doctor (other answers: choice of treatment or drug dosage, interpretation of laboratory results).
